scenario.summary: Attackers target unpatched vulnerabilities in End-of-Life (EoL) IoT devices, such as routers, cameras, and smart controllers, to gain initial network access. Once compromised, these devices are used to pivot into internal networks, redirect users to phishing sites, or are conscripted into large-scale botnets like Mozi and BADBOX 2.0.

meta.rationale: Target IoT-specific VLANs, guest networks, and industrial control subnets first. Focus the lead query on these zones to minimize noise from enterprise IT equipment.
meta.hypothesis: End-of-life IoT devices have been conscripted into botnets or hijacked for traffic redirection, evidenced by anomalous DNS failure patterns, internal lateral probing, or HTTP connections to phishing infrastructure.

blind_spots.question: whether the device is communicating with other hosts on the same L2 subnet
blind_spots.remediation: Deploy network sensors at the access layer or use private VLANs to force all traffic through a monitored point.

blind_spots.risk: Without agent coverage, identifying the physical device for remediation is delayed, extending the window of risk.
blind_spots.question: what the specific model and owner are for the identified suspicious IP
blind_spots.requires: accurate CMDB or MAC OUI integration
blind_spots.remediation: Integrate DHCP fingerprinting or MAC OUI lookups into the central telemetry lake.

blind_spots.risk: If the botnet uses DoH, the lead query will be silent, and the compromise will only be visible in later behavioral stages.
blind_spots.question: whether the botnet is using DNS-over-HTTPS to hide C2 lookups
blind_spots.remediation: Block outbound DoH traffic from IoT subnets and enforce internal DNS resolution.

hunt.name: Compromised IoT Network Activity
hunt.description: This hunt identifies the network-level behaviors of unmanaged IoT devices that have been compromised. It uses a gated flow, starting with a lead query that identifies hosts with high DNS failure rates, which often indicates botnet C2 or DGA activity. Only when these leads are verified does the hunt pivot into expensive behavioral analysis to find evidence of lateral movement (internal port scanning) and initial access redirection (phishing traffic). The hunt is designed for devices that lack endpoint agents by focusing on network telemetry surfaces.

config.beyond_detection: This hunt uses a gated flow to correlate DNS failure patterns with follow-on behavioral evidence. A single rule would only catch a static domain; this hunt identifies the pivot from C2 failure to internal lateral movement across multiple telemetry surfaces.

config.content: SELECT src_endpoint_ip, COUNT(*) as fail_count, COUNT(DISTINCT query_hostname) as unique_domains, MIN(time) as first_seen, MAX(time) as last_seen FROM hb_dns_activity WHERE rcode IN ('NXDOMAIN', 'SERVFAIL') AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days') GROUP BY src_endpoint_ip HAVING fail_count > 50 ORDER BY fail_count DESC
config.description: Identify internal IPs generating a high volume of NXDOMAIN or SERVFAIL responses, suggesting automated C2 or DGA attempts.
config.expected_signal: A list of IPs with persistent lookup failures. Silence suggests no heavy automated C2 activity is visible on this surface.

primitive_config.label: Lead: High DNS failure volume
primitive_config.content: SELECT src_endpoint_ip, COUNT(*) as fail_count, COUNT(DISTINCT query_hostname) as unique_domains, MIN(time) as first_seen, MAX(time) as last_seen FROM hb_dns_activity WHERE rcode IN ('NXDOMAIN', 'SERVFAIL') AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days') GROUP BY src_endpoint_ip HAVING fail_count > 50 ORDER BY fail_count DESC
primitive_config.expected: A list of IPs with persistent lookup failures. Silence suggests no heavy automated C2 activity is visible on this surface.

config.objective: Review the DNS lookup failures and determine if the frequency and target domains suggest an automated botnet agent.
config.description: Decide if the DNS failure pattern indicates a likely IoT botnet conscription.
config.expected_signal: A per-IP verdict classifying the behavior as suspicious or benign.
config.success_criteria: A verdict for each IP citing specific failure counts.

config.question: the evaluate-dns-lead verdict is suspicious for at least one host
config.condition: the evaluate-dns-lead verdict is suspicious for at least one host
config.description: Restrict expensive behavioral queries to only those environments showing suspicious DNS signals.

config.content: SELECT src_endpoint_ip, dst_endpoint_port, COUNT(DISTINCT dst_endpoint_ip) as internal_targets, MIN(time) as first_seen, MAX(time) as last_seen FROM hb_network_connection WHERE direction = 'outbound' AND ('{{scope_hosts}}' = '' OR instr(',' || '{{scope_hosts}}' || ',', ',' || src_endpoint_ip || ',') > 0) AND instr(',' || '{{management_ports}}' || ',', ',' || CAST(dst_endpoint_port AS TEXT) || ',') > 0 AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days') GROUP BY src_endpoint_ip, dst_endpoint_port HAVING internal_targets > 5 ORDER BY internal_targets DESC
config.description: Detect anomalous internal scanning of management ports originating from the suspicious IPs.
config.expected_signal: One IP hitting multiple internal targets on ports like 23 (Telnet) or 5555 (ADB).

primitive_config.label: Internal management port probing
primitive_config.content: SELECT src_endpoint_ip, dst_endpoint_port, COUNT(DISTINCT dst_endpoint_ip) as internal_targets, MIN(time) as first_seen, MAX(time) as last_seen FROM hb_network_connection WHERE direction = 'outbound' AND ('{{scope_hosts}}' = '' OR instr(',' || '{{scope_hosts}}' || ',', ',' || src_endpoint_ip || ',') > 0) AND instr(',' || '{{management_ports}}' || ',', ',' || CAST(dst_endpoint_port AS TEXT) || ',') > 0 AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days') GROUP BY src_endpoint_ip, dst_endpoint_port HAVING internal_targets > 5 ORDER BY internal_targets DESC
primitive_config.expected: One IP hitting multiple internal targets on ports like 23 (Telnet) or 5555 (ADB).

config.content: SELECT src_endpoint_ip, url_hostname, user_agent, COUNT(*) as req_count, MIN(time) as first_seen FROM hb_http_activity WHERE ('{{scope_hosts}}' = '' OR instr(',' || '{{scope_hosts}}' || ',', ',' || src_endpoint_ip || ',') > 0) AND instr(',' || '{{phishing_indicators}}' || ',', ',' || LOWER(url_hostname) || ',') > 0 AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days') GROUP BY src_endpoint_ip, url_hostname, user_agent ORDER BY req_count DESC
config.description: Identify HTTP requests to known phishing domains, indicating a hijacked IoT gateway or router.
config.expected_signal: Connections to phishing infrastructure from internal IPs.
